rows.req: Reporting rules never hard-coded in transaction logic
rows.ev: packages/accounting/src/statutory.ts, statutory-report.ts; tests/unit/architecture.test.ts ('no transaction module reads the reporting framework', 'statutory statements read the ledger and the reporting framework only', 'one writer per side'); tests/api/statutory.test.ts
rows.note: Statements and validations come only from the framework tables; disclosure rules are stored as data and rendered in V2-M5 from the same tables. The expression interpreter has no code evaluation (architecture-tested).
rows.accept: Statements, notes and validations come only from framework tables; an architecture test fails if transaction modules read them or if the report service reads source documents (ADR-63).

rows.req: Standard -> effective date -> reporting map -> disclosure rules -> validation rules
rows.ev: migration 20260119000000_v2_reporting_framework; tests/api/statutory.test.ts ('a second standard with another layout ... when the year switches to it')
rows.note: Standard, effective-dated version, statement lines, map, disclosure rules and validation rules are tables keyed to the version; company_reporting_framework selects one per financial year; switching the year's version changed the output with no code change.
rows.accept: Each layer is a table keyed to an effective-dated standard version; a company's financial year selects one version; changing the version changes the output without code.

rows.req: Support FRS 102, FRS 105 and future standards without redesign
rows.ev: tests/golden/v2-m1-micro-synthetic.json (version and alternative); tests/api/statutory.test.ts
rows.note: Two synthetic standards with different layouts produce their own hand-calculated statements from one ledger. A third standard is a further set of API calls (no code path names a standard). No real FRS 102 or FRS 105 content is entered (DEC-052).
rows.accept: Two synthetic standards with different layouts produce their own statements from the same ledger in tests; a third is added as data only.

rows.req: Every standard rule sourced and verified by a second person; unverified rules give previews only
rows.ev: tests/api/statutory.test.ts ('verification by a second person'); tests/db/reporting-framework.test.ts ('verification: once, by a person other than the author ...')
rows.note: Built and tested: author cannot verify (service 403 and database CHECK), verified version and its content immutable (service 409 and database trigger), changes supersede, unverified previews carry verified=false and a PREVIEW ONLY notice. Remaining: the filing-ready refusal of unverified rules lands with V2-M6. No real rule is verified until the firm names its qualified accountant.
rows.accept: Author cannot verify (service and database); verified records immutable; a change supersedes; previews carry verified=false and a notice; filing-ready output refuses unverified rules (V2-M6).

rows.req: Tax and reporting rules are effective-dated/versioned
rows.ev: migration 20260119000000_v2_reporting_framework; tests/api/statutory.test.ts ('a change supersedes ... the earlier year keeps the version it was prepared under, and its figures')
rows.note: Mechanism only: reporting maps are in the database per effective-dated, sourced version with verification status; after a later version replaced it, the 2025 preview still came from the version 2025 chose, with the same figures. V1 management statements keep the code registry (ADR-48). The rules the firm enters remain its own and unverified until its accountant verifies them (DEC-052).
rows.accept: Reporting maps effective-dated in the database with source and verification status (decided in DEC-051); a test proves a later version does not alter an earlier year's output.
The 14-step workflow (V2-YE rows) guides a financial year from lock to filing-ready package, each step showing its status from the underlying control.

rows.ev: tests/api/statutory.test.ts (golden: unplacedAccounts empty; broken map lists the bank loan); tests/db/reporting-framework.test.ts (unique map entry and active override)
rows.note: An override wins, else the most specific map entry, else the generic one (DEC-055). Double mapping cannot occur: the database allows one live entry per (version, V1 line, subtype) and one active override per account; the preview lists unmapped and misplaced accounts and proves the P&L against the ledger and the balance sheet to zero.
rows.accept: Every account of the trial balance lands on exactly one statutory line through the map or an override; unmapped and doubly mapped accounts are listed.

rows.note: Runs post through the PostingService (FIXED_ASSET_DEPRECIATION): one journal, a pair of lines per class, one line per asset. A run must be later than every live run, one live run per date. rows.ev: tests/golden/v2-m3a-adjustments.json (docs/architecture/v2-m3a-golden-workings.xlsx recomputes all 51 figures independently: 0 differences); tests/api/year-end.test.ts; tests/platform/year-end.test.ts; tests/db/year-end.test.ts

rows.req: Year-end closing journal to retained earnings
rows.ev: tests/golden/v2-m3b-close.json (docs/architecture/v2-m3b-golden-workings.xlsx recomputes all 152 figures independently: 0 differences); tests/api/year-end-close.test.ts; tests/platform/year-end-close.test.ts; tests/db/year-end-close.test.ts; tests/api/statutory.test.ts (preview unchanged by closes)
rows.note: Added 2026-10-18 from the approved plan (DEC-059). Built in V2-M3b (DEC-060): one closing journal per financial year (aligned to accounting periods, at most 18 months, never overlapping a live close) moves every income and expense balance of the year to retained earnings; while it is live the PostingService and the database refuse income and expense dated in the year; it is corrected only by its mirror. The management P&L, the balance sheet lines, the statutory preview and the FX report leave closing journals out and read the same before and after a close; the trial balance and the balance sheet's trial-balance proof include them.
rows.accept: The year's income and expense balances are closed to the retained-earnings account by one journal at the year end, reversible only by its mirror; every P&L figure (management P&L, statutory preview, FX report) excludes closing journals, and balance sheets include them, so statements reconcile before and after the close.
Director loan accounts per person with movements and the year-end balance; overdrawn balances and large movements flagged.
Related parties recorded with relationship and transactions for the year, available to the notes.
